# Workflow 01: First Import

Turn raw manuscript and notes into an organized canon-driven project.

## When to Use This

- You have a manuscript draft (full novel, partial chapters, scenes) sitting in some folder.
- You have a pile of notes — character sketches, world-building, plot ideas — scattered across files.
- You want the AI to convert all of that into a canon-driven project structure.

This is the **one-time bootstrap** workflow. After this runs successfully, use Workflow 02 (Incremental Update) for ongoing additions.

## Prerequisites

1. Project folder exists with the canon-driven structure (copy `templates/` or use one of the AI instruction files to create it).
2. Materials are in `_INBOX/`.
3. AI instructions file (`CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / etc.) is at the project root.

## The Prompt

Give your AI this:

```txt
Run an initial project import.

Read everything in `_INBOX/` without modifying the source files.

For each piece of information, classify it as CONFIRMED (directly stated in source), 
INFERRED (reasonably deduced), or TODO_CONFIRM (unclear / needs author decision).

Create or populate these files:

- 00_meta/project_index.md
- 00_meta/source_log.md
- 01_theme/theme.md
- 02_logline/logline.md
- 03_project_design/project_design.md
- 04_chapter_design/arc_index.md
- 90_canon/canon.md
- 90_canon/character_bible.md
- 93_exports/handoff_brief.md

Do not invent facts. Mark gaps as TODO_CONFIRM.

When done, update 00_meta/ai_work_log.md with what you processed, what you created, 
and what remains unclear. Suggest one specific next action.
```

## Expected Outputs

- `00_meta/project_index.md` — high-level table of what's where
- `00_meta/source_log.md` — every raw file from `_INBOX/` listed with brief notes
- `01_theme/theme.md` — what the story is fundamentally about
- `02_logline/logline.md` — protagonist, want, obstacle, hook
- `03_project_design/project_design.md` — concept, central experience, ongoing rewards
- `04_chapter_design/arc_index.md` — full series structure
- `90_canon/canon.md` — confirmed master canon
- `90_canon/character_bible.md` — character index and calling rules
- `93_exports/handoff_brief.md` — handoff stub for later use

## Pass Order

Internally the AI will work in this order:

1. **Source inventory** — list every file in `_INBOX/`, briefly describe each
2. **Rough project summary** — what is this project, roughly?
3. **Canon extraction** — extract only `CONFIRMED` facts to `90_canon/`
4. **Chapter / scene detection** — identify structural divisions in the manuscript
5. **Theme and logline extraction** — what's the story actually about?
6. **Open questions** — gather all `TODO_CONFIRM` items
7. **Work log** — record everything for the next session

## When This Workflow Goes Wrong

- **The AI invents facts** → reject the output, re-run with stronger emphasis on the no-invention rule.
- **The AI overwrites source material** → roll back from `_INBOX/` (which should still be intact); re-instruct the AI to never modify `_INBOX/`.
- **The output is too thin** → the input materials may be too sparse for a full bootstrap. Add more reference material to `_INBOX/` and re-run.
- **The AI gets stuck on length** → for very long manuscripts (>50k words), tell the AI to work in passes: source inventory first, then canon extraction, then chapter detection, etc. One pass at a time.

## After This Workflow

You now have a working project structure. Move to:

- **Workflow 02 (Incremental Update)** — when adding new material to an existing project.
- **Workflow 04 (Canon Audit)** — to find contradictions in what you've built.
- The **production pipeline** (multi-agent chapter writing) — see `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md` if you're now ready to draft new chapters.

# Canon

The master index and final-arbiter file for canonical facts about the story.

If something is contested across other canon files, the value in **this** file wins.
Most canonical facts should live in their specialized files (`character_bible.md`, `world_bible.md`, etc.). This file is for cross-cutting decisions, story-level facts, and the authoritative pointer to where everything else lives.

---

## Canonical Policy

- **Canon-promoted decisions** are locked. Agents cannot override them. To change canon, a human author must edit the source file.
- **Provisional decisions** are decisions made during drafting that may still change. Use `Provisional (YYYY-MM-DD)` markers in the source files.
- **Source-of-truth precedence (high → low)**:
  1. This file (`canon.md`)
  2. Specialized canon files (`character_bible.md`, `world_bible.md`, `glossary.md`, `timeline.md`)
  3. Style engine (`style_guide.md`, `forbidden_patterns.md`)
  4. Per-arc design files
  5. Per-chapter scene cards and briefs
  6. The drafts themselves (lowest authority — drafts are output, not source)

---

## Story-Level Canon

The handful of facts that define what makes this story THIS story. If you change any of these, you're writing a different story.

- **Genre / hybrid**: <e.g. "reincarnation fantasy with misperception comedy">
- **Core premise (one sentence)**: <the elevator pitch>
- **Protagonist's defining wound / drive**: <one sentence>
- **The promise to the reader**: <what you guarantee the story will deliver>
- **The thing you won't do**: <one or two anti-promises — what this story will NEVER become>

---

## Cross-File Indexing

Pointers to where specific canonical info lives:

| Topic | Lives in |
|---|---|
| Character names, roles, calling rules | `character_bible.md` |
| Detailed character voice and speech | `../03_project_design/characters/<NAME>.md` (if exists) |
| Locations, magic system, institutions | `world_bible.md` |
| Terminology and proper nouns | `glossary.md` |
| In-world dates and event sequence | `timeline.md` |
| Prose style rules | `../92_style_engine/style_guide.md` |
| Banned constructions and AI-tells | `../92_style_engine/forbidden_patterns.md` |

---

## Canon Change Log

Every promotion from Provisional → Canon, every demotion, every contested-then-resolved decision goes here:

| Date | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| YYYY-MM-DD | <e.g. "Character X's calling pattern in private with Y: promoted to Canon"> | <reason> |
| YYYY-MM-DD | <change> | <reason> |

This log is for human review during arc-end canon passes. It is NOT loaded into agent context (would bloat too fast).

---

## Hard Rules (story-specific things agents must never do)

This section is where you encode the project's non-negotiables. Things that can't be expressed cleanly in `forbidden_patterns.md` (because they're not patterns, they're story facts).

Examples:

- "Character X never reveals their true name in dialogue."
- "The enemy faction's existence is not narrated directly in the protagonist's POV before chapter 60."
- "Magic system rule: no character can use [specific ability] without paying [specific cost]. Any draft that does is wrong."
- "[Character Y] is dead from chapter 15 onward and cannot appear except in flashback or as a corpse."

---

## How Agents Use This File

- **All agents** read `canon.md` first when given a task. It tells them which other files to consult and which non-negotiables apply.
- **Canon review lens** uses the Hard Rules section as a checklist against the draft.
- **Brief agent** uses the Story-Level Canon to keep every chapter aligned with the story's defining promises.

# Character Bible

This is the canonical source of truth for every character in the story.
Names, roles, and calling patterns established here are treated as ground truth by every agent in the pipeline.

Detailed character notes (deep backstory, voice samples, behavioral DNA) can live in separate per-character files; this bible is the index.

---

## Characters

| Name | Role | First Appearance | Canon Status |
|---|---|---:|---|
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <one-line role description, e.g. "protagonist; reincarnator who believes he's a doomed background character"> | ch1 | Canon |
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <role> | ch3 | Canon |
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <role> | ch12 | Provisional (added YYYY-MM-DD) |

**Canon Status values:**
- `Canon` — Locked. Agents treat this as ground truth.
- `Provisional` — Recently added; may still change. Flag for review on next canon pass.
- `Deprecated` — No longer in active use; kept for historical reference.

---

## Houses / Organizations

| Name | Role | Canon Status |
|---|---|---|
| <HOUSE NAME> | <role, e.g. "protagonist's family; first protective sphere"> | Canon |
| <ORGANIZATION NAME> | <role, e.g. "measurement & external evaluation body"> | Canon |

---

## Calling Patterns

How each character is addressed. Crucial for voice consistency — agents will follow these patterns.

| Character | Main Calling Pattern |
|---|---|
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <e.g. "name; 'young master' (servants); 'name-sama' (formal)"> |
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <pattern> |

---

## Inter-Character Calling Rules

When two specific characters are in the same scene, how do they call each other? This often varies by context (public/private, formal/casual, who else is present).

| Speaker | Target | Calling | Context |
|---|---|---|---|
| <CHAR A> | <CHAR B> | <e.g. "family name"> | Public / first meeting / third parties present |
| <CHAR A> | <CHAR B> | <e.g. "given name + diminutive"> | Private / once they become close |
| <CHAR B> | <CHAR A> | <calling> | <context> |

These rules are the single biggest source of voice-consistency violations when AI drafts dialogue. Be exhaustive here — every "wait, would she actually call him that in front of his father?" question should be answerable from this table.

---

## Special Naming Conventions (story-specific)

If your story uses layered naming (e.g. a character has a true name, a public title, an enemy-faction nickname, and a reader-known alias), document the layer-to-speaker mapping here.

Example:

| Speaker / Layer | Calling |
|---|---|
| Enemy faction (internal) | "the dark child" |
| Royal court (formal) | "the strategic subject" |
| Protagonist's allies | his actual name |
| Protagonist himself | his actual name (he doesn't know about the other layers) |

This is how you prevent layer leakage — e.g. the protagonist's own POV chapter should never accidentally use the enemy faction's nickname for him.

---

## How Agents Use This File

- **Brief agent** extracts only the active characters for the chapter being drafted, plus the relevant calling rules, and includes them in the prose prompt as `MUST-INCLUDE` constraints.
- **Character review lens** loads this file alongside the chapter draft and flags any calling-pattern violations.
- **Canon review lens** flags any character action or attribute that contradicts the role description here.

- `INFERRED`: reasonably inferred, but not directly stated

### 3. Do not invent canon

If something is missing, mark it as missing.
Do not fill gaps with your own story ideas unless the user asks for ideation.

### 4. Do not flatten the project

Keep these categories separate:

- theme
- logline
- project design
- chapter design
- scene cards
- plot
- draft
- review
- revision
- canon
- reader emotion design
- character operating system

After each major operation, append a short entry to:

`00_meta/ai_work_log.md`

- date/time if available
- files read
- files created/updated
- assumptions
- unresolved questions

## Classification Rules

### `01_theme/` — when the material answers:

- What is this story really about?
- What emotional wound or desire powers it?
- What promise does the story make to the reader?
- What motifs repeat?

### `02_logline/` — when the material answers:

- Who is the protagonist?
- What do they want?
- What blocks them?
- What is the hook?
- Why should a reader care now?

### `03_project_design/` — when the material answers:

- What is the world?
- What are the rules?
- Who are the major characters?
- What is the genre contract?
- What must never be contradicted?

### `04_chapter_design/` — when the material answers:

- What is each chapter's purpose?
- What changes from start to end?
- What information is revealed?
- What reader emotion should the chapter produce?

### `05_scene_cards/` — when the material answers:

- Where does the scene happen?
- Who appears?
- What changes in the scene?
- What is the conflict?
- What is the scene's reader effect?

### `06_plot/` — when the material answers:

- What happens in order?
- What causes what?
- What setups and payoffs exist?
- What twists or reveals are planned?

### `07_draft/` — when the material is prose:

- Full manuscript
- Chapter text
- Scene text
- Dialogue draft
- Alternate draft

### `08_review/` — when the material evaluates:

- Strengths and weaknesses
- Reader experience
- Continuity problems
- Pacing problems
- Emotional curve problems

### `09_revision/` — when the material changes future work:

- Revision plan
- Rewrite instructions
- Patch list
- Before/after notes
- Revised draft copies

### `90_canon/` — when the material is confirmed in-world truth:

- Names, timeline, relationship facts
- Magic/system rules
- Backstory facts
- Glossary
- Open canon questions

### `91_jet_engine/` — when the material concerns reader emotion:

- Competence pleasure, injustice stress, dominance/justice reward
- Empathic investment, anticipatory reward, safety buffer
- Payoff timing, catharsis curve
- See [`docs/JET_OS_PRIMER.md`](../docs/JET_OS_PRIMER.md) at the repository root for full framework

### `03_project_design/characters/` — when the material concerns character behavior logic:

- Values, drives, flaws, trauma
- Attachment, threat level, growth pattern
- Relationship forces
- Voice samples (or place them in `92_style_engine/character_voice_samples.md`)

### `92_style_engine/` — when the material concerns prose-level rules:

- Style guide (POV, tense, register, sentence rhythm, punctuation conventions)
- Forbidden patterns (3-layer structure: surface grep / structural regex / semantic agent review)
- Character voice samples (concrete dialogue and internal-monologue excerpts per character)
- Generation prompts that target a specific prose feel

These files are read by the prose agent (samples and style guide) and by lint passes (forbidden patterns).

### `93_data/` — when the material is market analysis or reference:

- Platform ranking analysis, genre market data
- Title/tag optimization research
- Prior-work analysis, competitor analysis
- Reference excerpts (mind copyright on others' published text)

### `93_exports/` — when the material is for handoff:

- AI context pack
- Editorial summary
- Submission summary
- Next-agent brief
- Publication prep checklist

---

## Standard Commands

The user may write these commands in natural language. Treat them as operational modes.

### Initial Organization

Read `_INBOX/`, create or update project files, and produce a short report.

### Incremental Update

Only process newly added or changed materials. Update logs.

### Manuscript Decomposition

Split manuscript into chapters/scenes and create scene cards.

### Canon Extraction

Extract confirmed facts into `90_canon/` without inventing missing details.

### JET Diagnostic

Analyze reader emotion curve and write results to `91_jet_engine/` and `08_review/`.

### Character OS Extraction

Extract character behavior parameters into `03_project_design/characters/` (or `92_style_engine/character_voice_samples.md` for voice-only data).

### Revision Plan

Create a revision plan in `09_revision/` based on reviews and canon.

### Handoff Brief

Create a concise handoff brief in `93_exports/`.

---

## Output Style

When creating or updating files:

- Use Markdown.
- Prefer tables for registries.
- Use bullet points for quick scans.
- Use `CONFIRMED / INFERRED / TODO_CONFIRM` labels.
- Keep prose clear and practical.
- Do not over-explain obvious things.

When reporting to the user:

1. Say what you processed.
2. Say what you created/updated.
3. Say what remains unclear.
4. Suggest one next action, not many.

---

## Safety for Long Projects

For long manuscripts:

- Work in passes.
- Do not try to solve everything in one file.
- First create indexes and summaries.
- Then extract canon.
- Then create scene cards.
- Then review.
- Then revise.

Preferred order:

1. Source inventory
2. Project overview
3. Canon registry
4. Chapter map
5. Scene cards
6. JET audit
7. Character OS
8. Revision plan
9. Handoff brief

---

## Final Principle

The author owns the story.
You organize the project so the author and future AI agents can work without losing the story's core.

Official workflow:
# Workflow 02: Incremental Update

Add new material to an existing project without breaking what's already there.

## When to Use This

- The project has been bootstrapped (Workflow 01 already ran).
- You've added new files to `_INBOX/` since the last AI session.
- You don't want the AI to re-process everything from scratch.

This is the **ongoing maintenance** workflow. Use it every time you add manuscript chapters, new character notes, world-building updates, or new review feedback.

## The Prompt

```txt
Run an incremental update.

Process only NEW or CHANGED material in `_INBOX/` (check against `00_meta/source_log.md` 
for what's already been processed).

For each new piece of information:

1. Classify as CONFIRMED / INFERRED / TODO_CONFIRM.
2. Append to the appropriate existing file in 90_canon/, 03_project_design/, 
   04_chapter_design/, etc. — do not silently overwrite previous conclusions.
3. If the new information CONTRADICTS existing canon, do NOT auto-resolve. 
   Record the conflict in 90_canon/unresolved_questions.md with both old and new 
   versions and a dated note.

Update:
- 00_meta/source_log.md — log new sources processed
- 00_meta/ai_work_log.md — log this session's work
- 90_canon/unresolved_questions.md — log any new contradictions

When done, suggest one specific next action.
```

## Critical Rules for This Workflow

| Rule | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **Don't reprocess the entire project unless explicitly asked.** | Wastes tokens; risks overwriting good prior decisions. |
| **Don't silently overwrite previous conclusions.** | Author's decisions are sacred; surface conflicts, don't resolve them unilaterally. |
| **Add dated notes when interpretation changes.** | Future you needs to know WHEN something changed. |
| **Flag contradictions in `unresolved_questions.md`, don't auto-resolve.** | Contradictions are a HUMAN decision, not an AI one. |

## When the AI Detects a Conflict

The expected behavior is:

```md
## CONFLICT — 2024-XX-XX
**Old (from 90_canon/character_bible.md, recorded YYYY-MM-DD):**
> Character X has blue eyes.

**New (from _INBOX/character_notes_v2.md):**
> Character X has gray eyes.

**Status:** TODO_CONFIRM — Author decision needed.
```

The AI should NOT pick one and update silently. It should log the conflict and wait for human input.

## After This Workflow

- Resolve any `TODO_CONFIRM` items the AI surfaced.
- Update canon files to reflect your decisions (or ask the AI to do it explicitly).
- Continue drafting / reviewing.

If conflicts pile up, run **Workflow 04 (Canon Audit)** to clean house.

# Canon

The master index and final-arbiter file for canonical facts about the story.

If something is contested across other canon files, the value in **this** file wins.
Most canonical facts should live in their specialized files (`character_bible.md`, `world_bible.md`, etc.). This file is for cross-cutting decisions, story-level facts, and the authoritative pointer to where everything else lives.

---

## Canonical Policy

- **Canon-promoted decisions** are locked. Agents cannot override them. To change canon, a human author must edit the source file.
- **Provisional decisions** are decisions made during drafting that may still change. Use `Provisional (YYYY-MM-DD)` markers in the source files.
- **Source-of-truth precedence (high → low)**:
  1. This file (`canon.md`)
  2. Specialized canon files (`character_bible.md`, `world_bible.md`, `glossary.md`, `timeline.md`)
  3. Style engine (`style_guide.md`, `forbidden_patterns.md`)
  4. Per-arc design files
  5. Per-chapter scene cards and briefs
  6. The drafts themselves (lowest authority — drafts are output, not source)

---

## Story-Level Canon

The handful of facts that define what makes this story THIS story. If you change any of these, you're writing a different story.

- **Genre / hybrid**: <e.g. "reincarnation fantasy with misperception comedy">
- **Core premise (one sentence)**: <the elevator pitch>
- **Protagonist's defining wound / drive**: <one sentence>
- **The promise to the reader**: <what you guarantee the story will deliver>
- **The thing you won't do**: <one or two anti-promises — what this story will NEVER become>

---

## Cross-File Indexing

Pointers to where specific canonical info lives:

| Topic | Lives in |
|---|---|
| Character names, roles, calling rules | `character_bible.md` |
| Detailed character voice and speech | `../03_project_design/characters/<NAME>.md` (if exists) |
| Locations, magic system, institutions | `world_bible.md` |
| Terminology and proper nouns | `glossary.md` |
| In-world dates and event sequence | `timeline.md` |
| Prose style rules | `../92_style_engine/style_guide.md` |
| Banned constructions and AI-tells | `../92_style_engine/forbidden_patterns.md` |

---

## Canon Change Log

Every promotion from Provisional → Canon, every demotion, every contested-then-resolved decision goes here:

| Date | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| YYYY-MM-DD | <e.g. "Character X's calling pattern in private with Y: promoted to Canon"> | <reason> |
| YYYY-MM-DD | <change> | <reason> |

This log is for human review during arc-end canon passes. It is NOT loaded into agent context (would bloat too fast).

---

## Hard Rules (story-specific things agents must never do)

This section is where you encode the project's non-negotiables. Things that can't be expressed cleanly in `forbidden_patterns.md` (because they're not patterns, they're story facts).

Examples:

- "Character X never reveals their true name in dialogue."
- "The enemy faction's existence is not narrated directly in the protagonist's POV before chapter 60."
- "Magic system rule: no character can use [specific ability] without paying [specific cost]. Any draft that does is wrong."
- "[Character Y] is dead from chapter 15 onward and cannot appear except in flashback or as a corpse."

---

## How Agents Use This File

- **All agents** read `canon.md` first when given a task. It tells them which other files to consult and which non-negotiables apply.
- **Canon review lens** uses the Hard Rules section as a checklist against the draft.
- **Brief agent** uses the Story-Level Canon to keep every chapter aligned with the story's defining promises.

# Character Bible

This is the canonical source of truth for every character in the story.
Names, roles, and calling patterns established here are treated as ground truth by every agent in the pipeline.

Detailed character notes (deep backstory, voice samples, behavioral DNA) can live in separate per-character files; this bible is the index.

---

## Characters

| Name | Role | First Appearance | Canon Status |
|---|---|---:|---|
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <one-line role description, e.g. "protagonist; reincarnator who believes he's a doomed background character"> | ch1 | Canon |
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <role> | ch3 | Canon |
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <role> | ch12 | Provisional (added YYYY-MM-DD) |

**Canon Status values:**
- `Canon` — Locked. Agents treat this as ground truth.
- `Provisional` — Recently added; may still change. Flag for review on next canon pass.
- `Deprecated` — No longer in active use; kept for historical reference.

---

## Houses / Organizations

| Name | Role | Canon Status |
|---|---|---|
| <HOUSE NAME> | <role, e.g. "protagonist's family; first protective sphere"> | Canon |
| <ORGANIZATION NAME> | <role, e.g. "measurement & external evaluation body"> | Canon |

---

## Calling Patterns

How each character is addressed. Crucial for voice consistency — agents will follow these patterns.

| Character | Main Calling Pattern |
|---|---|
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <e.g. "name; 'young master' (servants); 'name-sama' (formal)"> |
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <pattern> |

---

## Inter-Character Calling Rules

When two specific characters are in the same scene, how do they call each other? This often varies by context (public/private, formal/casual, who else is present).

| Speaker | Target | Calling | Context |
|---|---|---|---|
| <CHAR A> | <CHAR B> | <e.g. "family name"> | Public / first meeting / third parties present |
| <CHAR A> | <CHAR B> | <e.g. "given name + diminutive"> | Private / once they become close |
| <CHAR B> | <CHAR A> | <calling> | <context> |

These rules are the single biggest source of voice-consistency violations when AI drafts dialogue. Be exhaustive here — every "wait, would she actually call him that in front of his father?" question should be answerable from this table.

---

## Special Naming Conventions (story-specific)

If your story uses layered naming (e.g. a character has a true name, a public title, an enemy-faction nickname, and a reader-known alias), document the layer-to-speaker mapping here.

Example:

| Speaker / Layer | Calling |
|---|---|
| Enemy faction (internal) | "the dark child" |
| Royal court (formal) | "the strategic subject" |
| Protagonist's allies | his actual name |
| Protagonist himself | his actual name (he doesn't know about the other layers) |

This is how you prevent layer leakage — e.g. the protagonist's own POV chapter should never accidentally use the enemy faction's nickname for him.

---

## How Agents Use This File

- **Brief agent** extracts only the active characters for the chapter being drafted, plus the relevant calling rules, and includes them in the prose prompt as `MUST-INCLUDE` constraints.
- **Character review lens** loads this file alongside the chapter draft and flags any calling-pattern violations.
- **Canon review lens** flags any character action or attribute that contradicts the role description here.

Keep this file lean and authoritative. Long backstory and voice samples go in separate files (e.g. `character_voice_samples.md`).

Handoff brief\n\n---\n\n## Final Principle\n\nThe author owns the story.\nYou organize the project so the author and future AI agents can work without losing the story's core.\n", "sha256": "f451988ae5ecd4b1011a2478067c8f8d623bb4c8aee1ea79aa3be96015920bf4", "kind": "public_method", "upstream_git_blob": "d4bfb370aaf6aadbbbbd4915422e7ceac673d0d6"}, "author:templates/_workflows/02_incremental_update.md": {"text": "# Workflow 02: Incremental Update\n\nAdd new material to an existing project without breaking what's already there.\n\n## When to Use This\n\n- The project has been bootstrapped (Workflow 01 already ran).\n- You've added new files to `_INBOX/` since the last AI session.\n- You don't want the AI to re-process everything from scratch.\n\nThis is the **ongoing maintenance** workflow. Use it every time you add manuscript chapters, new character notes, world-building updates, or new review feedback.\n\n## The Prompt\n\n```txt\nRun an incremental update.\n\nProcess only NEW or CHANGED material in `_INBOX/` (check against `00_meta/source_log.md` \nfor what's already been processed).\n\nFor each new piece of information:\n\n1. Classify as CONFIRMED / INFERRED / TODO_CONFIRM.\n2. Append to the appropriate existing file in 90_canon/, 03_project_design/, \n   04_chapter_design/, etc. — do not silently overwrite previous conclusions.\n3. If the new information CONTRADICTS existing canon, do NOT auto-resolve. \n   Record the conflict in 90_canon/unresolved_questions.md with both old and new \n   versions and a dated note.\n\nUpdate:\n- 00_meta/source_log.md — log new sources processed\n- 00_meta/ai_work_log.md — log this session's work\n- 90_canon/unresolved_questions.md — log any new contradictions\n\nWhen done, suggest one specific next action.\n```\n\n## Critical Rules for This Workflow\n\n| Rule | Why it matters |\n|---|---|\n| **Don't reprocess the entire project unless explicitly asked.** | Wastes tokens; risks overwriting good prior decisions. |\n| **Don't silently overwrite previous conclusions.** | Author's decisions are sacred; surface conflicts, don't resolve them unilaterally. |\n| **Add dated notes when interpretation changes.** | Future you needs to know WHEN something changed. |\n| **Flag contradictions in `unresolved_questions.md`, don't auto-resolve.** | Contradictions are a HUMAN decision, not an AI one. |\n\n## When the AI Detects a Conflict\n\nThe expected behavior is:\n\n```md\n## CONFLICT — 2024-XX-XX\n**Old (from 90_canon/character_bible.md, recorded YYYY-MM-DD):**\n> Character X has blue eyes.\n\n**New (from _INBOX/character_notes_v2.md):**\n> Character X has gray eyes.\n\n**Status:** TODO_CONFIRM — Author decision needed.\n```\n\nThe AI should NOT pick one and update silently. It should log the conflict and wait for human input.\n\n## After This Workflow\n\n- Resolve any `TODO_CONFIRM` items the AI surfaced.\n- Update canon files to reflect your decisions (or ask the AI to do it explicitly).\n- Continue drafting / reviewing.\n\nIf conflicts pile up, run **Workflow 04 (Canon Audit)** to clean house.\n", "sha256": "068a25c1df1510443c0e3acdf61e6c37855be4dea2d7e1221414718208fbb1da", "kind": "public_method", "upstream_git_blob": "ae1c43eb249aa6fdbe7462bd6fd058222eb015fc"}, "author:templates/90_canon/canon.template.md": {"text": "# Canon\n\nThe master index and final-arbiter file for canonical facts about the story.\n\nIf something is contested across other canon files, the value in **this** file wins.\nMost canonical facts should live in their specialized files (`character_bible.md`, `world_bible.md`, etc.). This file is for cross-cutting decisions, story-level facts, and the authoritative pointer to where everything else lives.\n\n---\n\n## Canonical Policy\n\n- **Canon-promoted decisions** are locked. Agents cannot override them. To change canon, a human author must edit the source file.\n- **Provisional decisions** are decisions made during drafting that may still change. Use `Provisional (YYYY-MM-DD)` markers in the source files.\n- **Source-of-truth precedence (high → low)**:\n  1. This file (`canon.md`)\n  2. Specialized canon files (`character_bible.md`, `world_bible.md`, `glossary.md`, `timeline.md`)\n  3. Style engine (`style_guide.md`, `forbidden_patterns.md`)\n  4. Per-arc design files\n  5. Per-chapter scene cards and briefs\n  6. The drafts themselves (lowest authority — drafts are output, not source)\n\n---\n\n## Story-Level Canon\n\nThe handful of facts that define what makes this story THIS story. If you change any of these, you're writing a different story.\n\n- **Genre / hybrid**: <e.g. \"reincarnation fantasy with misperception comedy\">\n- **Core premise (one sentence)**: <the elevator pitch>\n- **Protagonist's defining wound / drive**: <one sentence>\n- **The promise to the reader**: <what you guarantee the story will deliver>\n- **The thing you won't do**: <one or two anti-promises — what this story will NEVER become>\n\n---\n\n## Cross-File Indexing\n\nPointers to where specific canonical info lives:\n\n| Topic | Lives in |\n|---|---|\n| Character names, roles, calling rules | `character_bible.md` |\n| Detailed character voice and speech | `../03_project_design/characters/<NAME>.md` (if exists) |\n| Locations, magic system, institutions | `world_bible.md` |\n| Terminology and proper nouns | `glossary.md` |\n| In-world dates and event sequence | `timeline.md` |\n| Prose style rules | `../92_style_engine/style_guide.md` |\n| Banned constructions and AI-tells | `../92_style_engine/forbidden_patterns.md` |\n\n---\n\n## Canon Change Log\n\nEvery promotion from Provisional → Canon, every demotion, every contested-then-resolved decision goes here:\n\n| Date | Change | Reason |\n|---|---|---|\n| YYYY-MM-DD | <e.g. \"Character X's calling pattern in private with Y: promoted to Canon\"> | <reason> |\n| YYYY-MM-DD | <change> | <reason> |\n\nThis log is for human review during arc-end canon passes. It is NOT loaded into agent context (would bloat too fast).\n\n---\n\n## Hard Rules (story-specific things agents must never do)\n\nThis section is where you encode the project's non-negotiables. Things that can't be expressed cleanly in `forbidden_patterns.md` (because they're not patterns, they're story facts).\n\nExamples:\n\n- \"Character X never reveals their true name in dialogue.\"\n- \"The enemy faction's existence is not narrated directly in the protagonist's POV before chapter 60.\"\n- \"Magic system rule: no character can use [specific ability] without paying [specific cost]. Any draft that does is wrong.\"\n- \"[Character Y] is dead from chapter 15 onward and cannot appear except in flashback or as a corpse.\"\n\n---\n\n## How Agents Use This File\n\n- **All agents** read `canon.md` first when given a task. It tells them which other files to consult and which non-negotiables apply.\n- **Canon review lens** uses the Hard Rules section as a checklist against the draft.\n- **Brief agent** uses the Story-Level Canon to keep every chapter aligned with the story's defining promises.\n", "sha256": "216c4abae6cb97303209385728802e0820a775c48c714ae5a476d837278e9960", "kind": "public_method", "upstream_git_blob": "b39055a63394ec8e738517a49160260ebb3b3e78"}, "author:templates/04_chapter_design/arc_index.template.md": {"text": "# Arc Index\n\nFull-series structural index.\n\n| Arc | Title | Episodes | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Series | <total>-chapter series structure | 1-<N> | Per-chapter <char count>, <arc count> × <chapters-per-arc> overall plan |\n| 01 | <Arc 1 title> | 1-<X> | <Arc 1 purpose> |\n| 02 | <Arc 2 title> | <X+1>-<Y> | <Arc 2 purpose> |\n| ... | ... | ... | ... |\n", "sha256": "3263fcd9d20dde3f714d6320704c7140a37fa838a702943efa3e91eda271688f", "kind": "public_method", "upstream_git_blob": "ca61ec8b7a65b42e721f8f32b297bd9d4f9f5bbd"}, "author:templates/90_canon/character_bible.template.md": {"text": "# Character Bible\n\nThis is the canonical source of truth for every character in the story.\nNames, roles, and calling patterns established here are treated as ground truth by every agent in the pipeline.\n\nDetailed character notes (deep backstory, voice samples, behavioral DNA) can live in separate per-character files; this bible is the index.\n\n---\n\n## Characters\n\n| Name | Role | First Appearance | Canon Status |\n|---|---|---:|---|\n| <CHARACTER NAME> | <one-line role description, e.g. \"protagonist; reincarnator who believes he's a doomed background character\"> | ch1 | Canon |\n| <CHARACTER NAME> | <role> | ch3 | Canon |\n| <CHARACTER NAME> | <role> | ch12 | Provisional (added YYYY-MM-DD) |\n\n**Canon Status values:**\n- `Canon` — Locked. Agents treat this as ground truth.\n- `Provisional` — Recently added; may still change. Flag for review on next canon pass.\n- `Deprecated` — No longer in active use; kept for historical reference.\n\n---\n\n## Houses / Organizations\n\n| Name | Role | Canon Status |\n|---|---|---|\n| <HOUSE NAME> | <role, e.g. \"protagonist's family; first protective sphere\"> | Canon |\n| <ORGANIZATION NAME> | <role, e.g. \"measurement & external evaluation body\"> | Canon |\n\n---\n\n## Calling Patterns\n\nHow each character is addressed. Crucial for voice consistency — agents will follow these patterns.\n\n| Character | Main Calling Pattern |\n|---|---|\n| <CHARACTER NAME> | <e.g. \"name; 'young master' (servants); 'name-sama' (formal)\"> |\n| <CHARACTER NAME> | <pattern> |\n\n---\n\n## Inter-Character Calling Rules\n\nWhen two specific characters are in the same scene, how do they call each other? This often varies by context (public/private, formal/casual, who else is present).\n\n| Speaker | Target | Calling | Context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| <CHAR A> | <CHAR B> | <e.g. \"family name\"> | Public / first meeting / third parties present |\n| <CHAR A> | <CHAR B> | <e.g. \"given name + diminutive\"> | Private / once they become close |\n| <CHAR B> | <CHAR A> | <calling> | <context> |\n\nThese rules are the single biggest source of voice-consistency violations when AI drafts dialogue. Be exhaustive here — every \"wait, would she actually call him that in front of his father?\" question should be answerable from this table.\n\n---\n\n## Special Naming Conventions (story-specific)\n\nIf your story uses layered naming (e.g. a character has a true name, a public title, an enemy-faction nickname, and a reader-known alias), document the layer-to-speaker mapping here.\n\nExample:\n\n| Speaker / Layer | Calling |\n|---|---|\n| Enemy faction (internal) | \"the dark child\" |\n| Royal court (formal) | \"the strategic subject\" |\n| Protagonist's allies | his actual name |\n| Protagonist himself | his actual name (he doesn't know about the other layers) |\n\nThis is how you prevent layer leakage — e.g. the protagonist's own POV chapter should never accidentally use the enemy faction's nickname for him.\n\n---\n\n## How Agents Use This File\n\n- **Brief agent** extracts only the active characters for the chapter being drafted, plus the relevant calling rules, and includes them in the prose prompt as `MUST-INCLUDE` constraints.\n- **Character review lens** loads this file alongside the chapter draft and flags any calling-pattern violations.\n- **Canon review lens** flags any character action or attribute that contradicts the role description here.\n\nKeep this file lean and authoritative. Long backstory and voice samples go in separate files (e.g. `character_voice_samples.md`).\n", "sha256": "41b942ccb391c0d7673809c844c9b37f8ab3f42af502c86d0b95b1865ddf17d9", "kind": "public_method", "upstream_git_blob": "8cc022cfa6952ca455e31d7c8fdc5eaeb3b7d39a"}, "project:AGENTS.md": {"text": "# CLAUDE.md\n\nYou are operating inside a canon-driven novel project (claude-novel-workflow style).\nYour job is to organize, preserve, audit, and prepare novel project materials for long-term AI-assisted creation.\n\nThis is not a general writing prompt.\nThis is a project operating system.\n\n---\n\n## Core Mission\n\nTransform messy novel materials into a stable folder structure without damaging the original text.\n\nYou must:\n\n1. Preserve all source materials.\n2. Separate confirmed facts from inference.\n3. Separate draft text from design notes.\n4. Separate review from revision.\n5. Maintain canon consistency.\n6. Leave clear logs for future AI agents and the human author.\n\n---\n\n## Absolute Rules\n\n### 1. Never overwrite source material\n\nFiles in `_INBOX/` and `07_draft/` are source or draft records.\nDo not delete them.\nDo not rewrite them unless the user explicitly asks for a revised copy.\n\nWhen revision is needed, create a new file in `09_revision/`.\n\n### 2. Do not mix facts and guesses\n\nUse three labels:\n\n- `CONFIRMED`: directly stated in source material\n- `INFERRED`: reasonably inferred, but not directly stated\n- `TODO_CONFIRM`: unclear or needs author decision\n\n### 3. Do not invent canon\n\nIf something is missing, mark it as missing.\nDo not fill gaps with your own story ideas unless the user asks for ideation.\n\n### 4. Do not flatten the project\n\nKeep these categories separate:\n\n- theme\n- logline\n- project design\n- chapter design\n- scene cards\n- plot\n- draft\n- review\n- revision\n- canon\n- reader emotion design\n- character operating system\n\n### 5. Always log work\n\nAfter each major operation, append a short entry to:\n\n`00_meta/ai_work_log.md`\n\nInclude:\n\n- date/time if available\n- files read\n- files created/updated\n- assumptions\n- unresolved questions\n\n---\n\n## Folder Map\n\n```txt\n_INBOX/             Raw files dropped by the user. Never modify.\n00_meta/            Project index, source log, AI work log, decision log.\n01_theme/           Theme, motifs, emotional core, promise to reader.\n02_logline/         Logline, pitch, target reader, hook variants.\n03_project_design/  Project bible: world, characters, rules, genre contract.\n04_chapter_design/  Chapter list, chapter purposes, volume arc.\n05_scene_cards/     Scene-level cards and scene index.\n06_plot/            Plot outline, cause-effect chain, foreshadowing map.\n07_draft/           Draft text, chapter drafts, imported manuscript.\n08_review/          Review reports, reader emotion audit, continuity audit.\n09_revision/        Revision plans and revised drafts.\n90_canon/           Confirmed facts, glossary, timeline, unresolved canon.\n91_jet_engine/      Reader emotion parameters and payoff design.\n                    (Character behavior logic lives in 03_project_design/characters/)\n92_style_engine/    Style guide, forbidden patterns, character voice samples.\n93_data/            Market data, reference materials, analysis.\n93_exports/         Handoff briefs, publication packs, AI summaries.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Classification Rules\n\n### `01_theme/` — when the material answers:\n\n- What is this story really about?\n- What emotional wound or desire powers it?\n- What promise does the story make to the reader?\n- What motifs repeat?\n\n### `02_logline/` — when the material answers:\n\n- Who is the protagonist?\n- What do they want?\n- What blocks them?\n- What is the hook?\n- Why should a reader care now?\n\n### `03_project_design/` — when the material answers:\n\n- What is the world?\n- What are the rules?\n- Who are the major characters?\n- What is the genre contract?\n- What must never be contradicted?\n\n### `04_chapter_design/` — when the material answers:\n\n- What is each chapter's purpose?\n- What changes from start to end?\n- What information is revealed?\n- What reader emotion should the chapter produce?\n\n### `05_scene_cards/` — when the material answers:\n\n- Where does the scene happen?\n- Who appears?\n- What changes in the scene?\n- What is the conflict?\n- What is the scene's reader effect?\n\n### `06_plot/` — when the material answers:\n\n- What happens in order?\n- What causes what?\n- What setups and payoffs exist?\n- What twists or reveals are planned?\n\n### `07_draft/` — when the material is prose:\n\n- Full manuscript\n- Chapter text\n- Scene text\n- Dialogue draft\n- Alternate draft\n\n### `08_review/` — when the material evaluates:\n\n- Strengths and weaknesses\n- Reader experience\n- Continuity problems\n- Pacing problems\n- Emotional curve problems\n\n### `09_revision/` — when the material changes future work:\n\n- Revision plan\n- Rewrite instructions\n- Patch list\n- Before/after notes\n- Revised draft copies\n\n### `90_canon/` — when the material is confirmed in-world truth:\n\n- Names, timeline, relationship facts\n- Magic/system rules\n- Backstory facts\n- Glossary\n- Open canon questions\n\n### `91_jet_engine/` — when the material concerns reader emotion:\n\n- Competence pleasure, injustice stress, dominance/justice reward\n- Empathic investment, anticipatory reward, safety buffer\n- Payoff timing, catharsis curve\n- See [`docs/JET_OS_PRIMER.md`](../docs/JET_OS_PRIMER.md) at the repository root for full framework\n\n### `03_project_design/characters/` — when the material concerns character behavior logic:\n\n- Values, drives, flaws, trauma\n- Attachment, threat level, growth pattern\n- Relationship forces\n- Voice samples (or place them in `92_style_engine/character_voice_samples.md`)\n\n### `92_style_engine/` — when the material concerns prose-level rules:\n\n- Style guide (POV, tense, register, sentence rhythm, punctuation conventions)\n- Forbidden patterns (3-layer structure: surface grep / structural regex / semantic agent review)\n- Character voice samples (concrete dialogue and internal-monologue excerpts per character)\n- Generation prompts that target a specific prose feel\n\nThese files are read by the prose agent (samples and style guide) and by lint passes (forbidden patterns).\n\n### `93_data/` — when the material is market analysis or reference:\n\n- Platform ranking analysis, genre market data\n- Title/tag optimization research\n- Prior-work analysis, competitor analysis\n- Reference excerpts (mind copyright on others' published text)\n\n### `93_exports/` — when the material is for handoff:\n\n- AI context pack\n- Editorial summary\n- Submission summary\n- Next-agent brief\n- Publication prep checklist\n\n---\n\n## Standard Commands\n\nThe user may write these commands in natural language. Treat them as operational modes.\n\n### Initial Organization\n\nRead `_INBOX/`, create or update project files, and produce a short report.\n\n### Incremental Update\n\nOnly process newly added or changed materials. Update logs.\n\n### Manuscript Decomposition\n\nSplit manuscript into chapters/scenes and create scene cards.\n\n### Canon Extraction\n\nExtract confirmed facts into `90_canon/` without inventing missing details.\n\n### JET Diagnostic\n\nAnalyze reader emotion curve and write results to `91_jet_engine/` and `08_review/`.\n\n### Character OS Extraction\n\nExtract character behavior parameters into `03_project_design/characters/` (or `92_style_engine/character_voice_samples.md` for voice-only data).\n\n### Revision Plan\n\nCreate a revision plan in `09_revision/` based on reviews and canon.\n\n### Handoff Brief\n\nCreate a concise handoff brief in `93_exports/`.\n\n---\n\n## Output Style\n\nWhen creating or updating files:\n\n- Use Markdown.\n- Prefer tables for registries.\n- Use bullet points for quick scans.\n- Use `CONFIRMED / INFERRED / TODO_CONFIRM` labels.\n- Keep prose clear and practical.\n- Do not over-explain obvious things.\n\nWhen reporting to the user:\n\n1. Say what you processed.\n2. Say what you created/updated.\n3. Say what remains unclear.\n4. Suggest one next action, not many.\n\n---\n\n## Safety for Long Projects\n\nFor long manuscripts:\n\n- Work in passes.\n- Do not try to solve everything in one file.\n- First create indexes and summaries.\n- Then extract canon.\n- Then create scene cards.\n- Then review.\n- Then revise.\n\nPreferred order:\n\n1. Source inventory\n2. Project overview\n3. Canon registry\n4. Chapter map\n5. Scene cards\n6. JET audit\n7. Character OS\n8. Revision plan\n9. Handoff brief\n\n---\n\n## Final Principle\n\nThe author owns the story.\nYou organize the project so the author and future AI agents can work without losing the story's core.\n", "sha256": You are operating inside a canon-driven novel project (claude-novel-workflow style).
Your job is to organize, preserve, audit, and prepare novel project materials for long-term AI-assisted creation.

This is not a general writing prompt.
This is a project operating system.

---

## Core Mission

Transform messy novel materials into a stable folder structure without damaging the original text.

You must:

1. Preserve all source materials.
2. Separate confirmed facts from inference.
3. Separate draft text from design notes.
4. Separate review from revision.
5. Maintain canon consistency.
6. Leave clear logs for future AI agents and the human author.

---

## Absolute Rules

### 1. Never overwrite source material

Files in `_INBOX/` and `07_draft/` are source or draft records.
Do not delete them.
Do not rewrite them unless the user explicitly asks for a revised copy.

When revision is needed, create a new file in `09_revision/`.

### 2. Do not mix facts and guesses

Use three labels:

- `CONFIRMED`: directly stated in source material
- `INFERRED`: reasonably inferred, but not directly stated
- `TODO_CONFIRM`: unclear or needs author decision

### 3. Do not invent canon

If something is missing, mark it as missing.
Do not fill gaps with your own story ideas unless the user asks for ideation.

### 4. Do not flatten the project

Keep these categories separate:

- theme
- logline
- project design
- chapter design
- scene cards
- plot
- draft
- review
- revision
- canon
- reader emotion design
- character operating system

### 5. Always log work

After each major operation, append a short entry to:

`00_meta/ai_work_log.md`

Include:

- date/time if available
- files read
- files created/updated
- assumptions
- unresolved questions

---

## Folder Map

```txt
_INBOX/             Raw files dropped by the user. Never modify.
00_meta/            Project index, source log, AI work log, decision log.
01_theme/           Theme, motifs, emotional core, promise to reader.
02_logline/         Logline, pitch, target reader, hook variants.
03_project_design/  Project bible: world, characters, rules, genre contract.
04_chapter_design/  Chapter list, chapter purposes, volume arc.
05_scene_cards/     Scene-level cards and scene index.
06_plot/            Plot outline, cause-effect chain, foreshadowing map.
07_draft/           Draft text, chapter drafts, imported manuscript.
08_review/          Review reports, reader emotion audit, continuity audit.
09_revision/        Revision plans and revised drafts.
90_canon/           Confirmed facts, glossary, timeline, unresolved canon.
91_jet_engine/      Reader emotion parameters and payoff design.
                    (Character behavior logic lives in 03_project_design/characters/)
92_style_engine/    Style guide, forbidden patterns, character voice samples.
93_data/            Market data, reference materials, analysis.
93_exports/         Handoff briefs, publication packs, AI summaries.
```

---

## Classification Rules

### `01_theme/` — when the material answers:

- What is this story really about?
- What emotional wound or desire powers it?
- What promise does the story make to the reader?
- What motifs repeat?

### `02_logline/` — when the material answers:

- Who is the protagonist?
- What do they want?
- What blocks them?
- What is the hook?
- Why should a reader care now?

### `03_project_design/` — when the material answers:

- What is the world?
- What are the rules?
- Who are the major characters?
- What is the genre contract?
- What must never be contradicted?

### `04_chapter_design/` — when the material answers:

- What is each chapter's purpose?
- What changes from start to end?
- What information is revealed?
- What reader emotion should the chapter produce?

### `05_scene_cards/` — when the material answers:

- Where does the scene happen?
- Who appears?
- What changes in the scene?
- What is the conflict?
- What is the scene's reader effect?

### `06_plot/` — when the material answers:

- What happens in order?
- What causes what?
- What setups and payoffs exist?
- What twists or reveals are planned?

### `07_draft/` — when the material is prose:

- Full manuscript
- Chapter text
- Scene text
- Dialogue draft
- Alternate draft

### `08_review/` — when the material evaluates:

- Strengths and weaknesses
- Reader experience
- Continuity problems
- Pacing problems
- Emotional curve problems

### `09_revision/` — when the material changes future work:

- Revision plan
- Rewrite instructions
- Patch list
- Before/after notes
- Revised draft copies

### `90_canon/` — when the material is confirmed in-world truth:

- Names, timeline, relationship facts
- Magic/system rules
- Backstory facts
- Glossary
- Open canon questions

### `91_jet_engine/` — when the material concerns reader emotion:

- Competence pleasure, injustice stress, dominance/justice reward
- Empathic investment, anticipatory reward, safety buffer
- Payoff timing, catharsis curve
- See [`docs/JET_OS_PRIMER.md`](../docs/JET_OS_PRIMER.md) at the repository root for full framework

### `03_project_design/characters/` — when the material concerns character behavior logic:

- Values, drives, flaws, trauma
- Attachment, threat level, growth pattern
- Relationship forces
- Voice samples (or place them in `92_style_engine/character_voice_samples.md`)

### `92_style_engine/` — when the material concerns prose-level rules:

- Style guide (POV, tense, register, sentence rhythm, punctuation conventions)
- Forbidden patterns (3-layer structure: surface grep / structural regex / semantic agent review)
- Character voice samples (concrete dialogue and internal-monologue excerpts per character)
- Generation prompts that target a specific prose feel

These files are read by the prose agent (samples and style guide) and by lint passes (forbidden patterns).

### `93_data/` — when the material is market analysis or reference:

- Platform ranking analysis, genre market data
- Title/tag optimization research
- Prior-work analysis, competitor analysis
- Reference excerpts (mind copyright on others' published text)

### `93_exports/` — when the material is for handoff:

- AI context pack
- Editorial summary
- Submission summary
- Next-agent brief
- Publication prep checklist

---

## Standard Commands

The user may write these commands in natural language. Treat them as operational modes.

### Initial Organization

Read `_INBOX/`, create or update project files, and produce a short report.

### Incremental Update

Only process newly added or changed materials. Update logs.

### Manuscript Decomposition

Split manuscript into chapters/scenes and create scene cards.

### Canon Extraction

Extract confirmed facts into `90_canon/` without inventing missing details.

### JET Diagnostic

Analyze reader emotion curve and write results to `91_jet_engine/` and `08_review/`.

### Character OS Extraction

Extract character behavior parameters into `03_project_design/characters/` (or `92_style_engine/character_voice_samples.md` for voice-only data).

### Revision Plan

Create a revision plan in `09_revision/` based on reviews and canon.

### Handoff Brief

Create a concise handoff brief in `93_exports/`.

---

## Output Style

When creating or updating files:

- Use Markdown.
- Prefer tables for registries.
- Use bullet points for quick scans.
- Use `CONFIRMED / INFERRED / TODO_CONFIRM` labels.
- Keep prose clear and practical.
- Do not over-explain obvious things.

When reporting to the user:

1. Say what you processed.
2. Say what you created/updated.
3. Say what remains unclear.
4. Suggest one next action, not many.

---

## Safety for Long Projects

For long manuscripts:

- Work in passes.
- Do not try to solve everything in one file.
- First create indexes and summaries.
- Then extract canon.
- Then create scene cards.
- Then review.
- Then revise.

Preferred order:

1. Source inventory
2. Project overview
3. Canon registry
4. Chapter map
5. Scene cards
6. JET audit
7. Character OS
8. Revision plan
9. Handoff brief

---

## Final Principle

The author owns the story.
You organize the project so the author and future AI agents can work without losing the story's core.

Official workflow:
# Workflow 02: Incremental Update

Add new material to an existing project without breaking what's already there.

## When to Use This

- The project has been bootstrapped (Workflow 01 already ran).
- You've added new files to `_INBOX/` since the last AI session.
- You don't want the AI to re-process everything from scratch.

This is the **ongoing maintenance** workflow. Use it every time you add manuscript chapters, new character notes, world-building updates, or new review feedback.

## The Prompt

```txt
Run an incremental update.

Process only NEW or CHANGED material in `_INBOX/` (check against `00_meta/source_log.md` 
for what's already been processed).

For each new piece of information:

1. Classify as CONFIRMED / INFERRED / TODO_CONFIRM.
2. Append to the appropriate existing file in 90_canon/, 03_project_design/, 
   04_chapter_design/, etc. — do not silently overwrite previous conclusions.
3. If the new information CONTRADICTS existing canon, do NOT auto-resolve. 
   Record the conflict in 90_canon/unresolved_questions.md with both old and new 
   versions and a dated note.

Update:
- 00_meta/source_log.md — log new sources processed
- 00_meta/ai_work_log.md — log this session's work
- 90_canon/unresolved_questions.md — log any new contradictions

When done, suggest one specific next action.
```

## Critical Rules for This Workflow

| Rule | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **Don't reprocess the entire project unless explicitly asked.** | Wastes tokens; risks overwriting good prior decisions. |
| **Don't silently overwrite previous conclusions.** | Author's decisions are sacred; surface conflicts, don't resolve them unilaterally. |
| **Add dated notes when interpretation changes.** | Future you needs to know WHEN something changed. |
| **Flag contradictions in `unresolved_questions.md`, don't auto-resolve.** | Contradictions are a HUMAN decision, not an AI one. |

## When the AI Detects a Conflict

The expected behavior is:

```md
## CONFLICT — 2024-XX-XX
**Old (from 90_canon/character_bible.md, recorded YYYY-MM-DD):**
> Character X has blue eyes.

**New (from _INBOX/character_notes_v2.md):**
> Character X has gray eyes.

**Status:** TODO_CONFIRM — Author decision needed.
```

The AI should NOT pick one and update silently. It should log the conflict and wait for human input.

## After This Workflow

- Resolve any `TODO_CONFIRM` items the AI surfaced.
- Update canon files to reflect your decisions (or ask the AI to do it explicitly).
- Continue drafting / reviewing.

If conflicts pile up, run **Workflow 04 (Canon Audit)** to clean house.

# Canon

The master index and final-arbiter file for canonical facts about the story.

If something is contested across other canon files, the value in **this** file wins.
Most canonical facts should live in their specialized files (`character_bible.md`, `world_bible.md`, etc.). This file is for cross-cutting decisions, story-level facts, and the authoritative pointer to where everything else lives.

---

## Canonical Policy

- **Canon-promoted decisions** are locked. Agents cannot override them. To change canon, a human author must edit the source file.
- **Provisional decisions** are decisions made during drafting that may still change. Use `Provisional (YYYY-MM-DD)` markers in the source files.
- **Source-of-truth precedence (high → low)**:
  1. This file (`canon.md`)
  2. Specialized canon files (`character_bible.md`, `world_bible.md`, `glossary.md`, `timeline.md`)
  3. Style engine (`style_guide.md`, `forbidden_patterns.md`)
  4. Per-arc design files
  5. Per-chapter scene cards and briefs
  6. The drafts themselves (lowest authority — drafts are output, not source)

---

## Story-Level Canon

The handful of facts that define what makes this story THIS story. If you change any of these, you're writing a different story.

- **Genre / hybrid**: <e.g. "reincarnation fantasy with misperception comedy">
- **Core premise (one sentence)**: <the elevator pitch>
- **Protagonist's defining wound / drive**: <one sentence>
- **The promise to the reader**: <what you guarantee the story will deliver>
- **The thing you won't do**: <one or two anti-promises — what this story will NEVER become>

---

## Cross-File Indexing

Pointers to where specific canonical info lives:

| Topic | Lives in |
|---|---|
| Character names, roles, calling rules | `character_bible.md` |
| Detailed character voice and speech | `../03_project_design/characters/<NAME>.md` (if exists) |
| Locations, magic system, institutions | `world_bible.md` |
| Terminology and proper nouns | `glossary.md` |
| In-world dates and event sequence | `timeline.md` |
| Prose style rules | `../92_style_engine/style_guide.md` |
| Banned constructions and AI-tells | `../92_style_engine/forbidden_patterns.md` |

---

## Canon Change Log

Every promotion from Provisional → Canon, every demotion, every contested-then-resolved decision goes here:

| Date | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| YYYY-MM-DD | <e.g. "Character X's calling pattern in private with Y: promoted to Canon"> | <reason> |
| YYYY-MM-DD | <change> | <reason> |

This log is for human review during arc-end canon passes. It is NOT loaded into agent context (would bloat too fast).

---

## Hard Rules (story-specific things agents must never do)

This section is where you encode the project's non-negotiables. Things that can't be expressed cleanly in `forbidden_patterns.md` (because they're not patterns, they're story facts).

Examples:

- "Character X never reveals their true name in dialogue."
- "The enemy faction's existence is not narrated directly in the protagonist's POV before chapter 60."
- "Magic system rule: no character can use [specific ability] without paying [specific cost]. Any draft that does is wrong."
- "[Character Y] is dead from chapter 15 onward and cannot appear except in flashback or as a corpse."

---

## How Agents Use This File

- **All agents** read `canon.md` first when given a task. It tells them which other files to consult and which non-negotiables apply.
- **Canon review lens** uses the Hard Rules section as a checklist against the draft.
- **Brief agent** uses the Story-Level Canon to keep every chapter aligned with the story's defining promises.

# Character Bible

This is the canonical source of truth for every character in the story.
Names, roles, and calling patterns established here are treated as ground truth by every agent in the pipeline.

Detailed character notes (deep backstory, voice samples, behavioral DNA) can live in separate per-character files; this bible is the index.

---

## Characters

| Name | Role | First Appearance | Canon Status |
|---|---|---:|---|
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <one-line role description, e.g. "protagonist; reincarnator who believes he's a doomed background character"> | ch1 | Canon |
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <role> | ch3 | Canon |
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <role> | ch12 | Provisional (added YYYY-MM-DD) |

**Canon Status values:**
- `Canon` — Locked. Agents treat this as ground truth.
- `Provisional` — Recently added; may still change. Flag for review on next canon pass.
- `Deprecated` — No longer in active use; kept for historical reference.

---

## Houses / Organizations

| Name | Role | Canon Status |
|---|---|---|
| <HOUSE NAME> | <role, e.g. "protagonist's family; first protective sphere"> | Canon |
| <ORGANIZATION NAME> | <role, e.g. "measurement & external evaluation body"> | Canon |

---

## Calling Patterns

How each character is addressed. Crucial for voice consistency — agents will follow these patterns.

| Character | Main Calling Pattern |
|---|---|
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <e.g. "name; 'young master' (servants); 'name-sama' (formal)"> |
| <CHARACTER NAME> | <pattern> |

---

## Inter-Character Calling Rules

When two specific characters are in the same scene, how do they call each other? This often varies by context (public/private, formal/casual, who else is present).

| Speaker | Target | Calling | Context |
|---|---|---|---|
| <CHAR A> | <CHAR B> | <e.g. "family name"> | Public / first meeting / third parties present |
| <CHAR A> | <CHAR B> | <e.g. "given name + diminutive"> | Private / once they become close |
| <CHAR B> | <CHAR A> | <calling> | <context> |

These rules are the single biggest source of voice-consistency violations when AI drafts dialogue. Be exhaustive here — every "wait, would she actually call him that in front of his father?" question should be answerable from this table.

---

## Special Naming Conventions (story-specific)

If your story uses layered naming (e.g. a character has a true name, a public title, an enemy-faction nickname, and a reader-known alias), document the layer-to-speaker mapping here.

Example:

| Speaker / Layer | Calling |
|---|---|
| Enemy faction (internal) | "the dark child" |
| Royal court (formal) | "the strategic subject" |
| Protagonist's allies | his actual name |
| Protagonist himself | his actual name (he doesn't know about the other layers) |

This is how you prevent layer leakage — e.g. the protagonist's own POV chapter should never accidentally use the enemy faction's nickname for him.

---

- **Brief agent** extracts only the active characters for the chapter being drafted, plus the relevant calling rules, and includes them in the prose prompt as `MUST-INCLUDE` constraints.
- **Character review lens** loads this file alongside the chapter draft and flags any calling-pattern violations.
- **Canon review lens** flags any character action or attribute that contradicts the role description here.

Use it every time you add manuscript chapters, new character notes, world-building updates, or new review feedback.\n\n## The Prompt\n\n```txt\nRun an incremental update.\n\nProcess only NEW or CHANGED material in `_INBOX/` (check against `00_meta/source_log.md` \nfor what's already been processed).\n\nFor each new piece of information:\n\n1. Classify as CONFIRMED / INFERRED / TODO_CONFIRM.\n2. Append to the appropriate existing file in 90_canon/, 03_project_design/, \n   04_chapter_design/, etc. — do not silently overwrite previous conclusions.\n3. If the new information CONTRADICTS existing canon, do NOT auto-resolve. \n   Record the conflict in 90_canon/unresolved_questions.md with both old and new \n   versions and a dated note.\n\nUpdate:\n- 00_meta/source_log.md — log new sources processed\n- 00_meta/ai_work_log.md — log this session's work\n- 90_canon/unresolved_questions.md — log any new contradictions\n\nWhen done, suggest one specific next action.\n```\n\n## Critical Rules for This Workflow\n\n| Rule | Why it matters |\n|---|---|\n| **Don't reprocess the entire project unless explicitly asked.** | Wastes tokens; risks overwriting good prior decisions. |\n| **Don't silently overwrite previous conclusions.** | Author's decisions are sacred; surface conflicts, don't resolve them unilaterally. |\n| **Add dated notes when interpretation changes.** | Future you needs to know WHEN something changed. |\n| **Flag contradictions in `unresolved_questions.md`, don't auto-resolve.** | Contradictions are a HUMAN decision, not an AI one. |\n\n## When the AI Detects a Conflict\n\nThe expected behavior is:\n\n```md\n## CONFLICT — 2024-XX-XX\n**Old (from 90_canon/character_bible.md, recorded YYYY-MM-DD):**\n> Character X has blue eyes.\n\n**New (from _INBOX/character_notes_v2.md):**\n> Character X has gray eyes.\n\n**Status:** TODO_CONFIRM — Author decision needed.\n```\n\nThe AI should NOT pick one and update silently. This file is for cross-cutting decisions, story-level facts, and the authoritative pointer to where everything else lives.\n\n---\n\n## Canonical Policy\n\n- **Canon-promoted decisions** are locked. Agents cannot override them. To change canon, a human author must edit the source file.\n- **Provisional decisions** are decisions made during drafting that may still change. Use `Provisional (YYYY-MM-DD)` markers in the source files.\n- **Source-of-truth precedence (high → low)**:\n  1. This file (`canon.md`)\n  2. Specialized canon files (`character_bible.md`, `world_bible.md`, `glossary.md`, `timeline.md`)\n  3. Style engine (`style_guide.md`, `forbidden_patterns.md`)\n  4. Per-arc design files\n  5. Per-chapter scene cards and briefs\n  6. The drafts themselves (lowest authority — drafts are output, not source)\n\n---\n\n## Story-Level Canon\n\nThe handful of facts that define what makes this story THIS story. If you change any of these, you're writing a different story.\n\n- **Genre / hybrid**: <e.g. \"reincarnation fantasy with misperception comedy\">\n- **Core premise (one sentence)**: <the elevator pitch>\n- **Protagonist's defining wound / drive**: <one sentence>\n- **The promise to the reader**: <what you guarantee the story will deliver>\n- **The thing you won't do**: <one or two anti-promises — what this story will NEVER become>\n\n---\n\n## Cross-File Indexing\n\nPointers to where specific canonical info lives:\n\n| Topic | Lives in |\n|---|---|\n| Character names, roles, calling rules | `character_bible.md` |\n| Detailed character voice and speech | `../03_project_design/characters/<NAME>.md` (if exists) |\n| Locations, magic system, institutions | `world_bible.md` |\n| Terminology and proper nouns | `glossary.md` |\n| In-world dates and event sequence | `timeline.md` |\n| Prose style rules | `../92_style_engine/style_guide.md` |\n| Banned constructions and AI-tells | `../92_style_engine/forbidden_patterns.md` |\n\n---\n\n## Canon Change Log\n\nEvery promotion from Provisional → Canon, every demotion, every contested-then-resolved decision goes here:\n\n| Date | Change | Reason |\n|---|---|---|\n| YYYY-MM-DD | <e.g. \"Character X's calling pattern in private with Y: promoted to Canon\"> | <reason> |\n| YYYY-MM-DD | <change> | <reason> |\n\nThis log is for human review during arc-end canon passes. It is NOT loaded into agent context (would bloat too fast).\n\n---\n\n## Hard Rules (story-specific things agents must never do)\n\nThis section is where you encode the project's non-negotiables. Things that can't be expressed cleanly in `forbidden_patterns.md` (because they're not patterns, they're story facts).\n\nExamples:\n\n- \"Character X never reveals their true name in dialogue.\"\n- \"The enemy faction's existence is not narrated directly in the protagonist's POV before chapter 60.\"\n- \"Magic system rule: no character can use [specific ability] without paying [specific cost]. Any draft that does is wrong.\"\n- \"[Character Y] is dead from chapter 15 onward and cannot appear except in flashback or as a corpse.\"\n\n---\n\n## How Agents Use This File\n\n- **All agents** read `canon.md` first when given a task. This often varies by context (public/private, formal/casual, who else is present).\n\n| Speaker | Target | Calling | Context |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| <CHAR A> | <CHAR B> | <e.g. \"family name\"> | Public / first meeting / third parties present |\n| <CHAR A> | <CHAR B> | <e.g. \"given name + diminutive\"> | Private / once they become close |\n| <CHAR B> | <CHAR A> | <calling> | <context> |\n\nThese rules are the single biggest source of voice-consistency violations when AI drafts dialogue.
